title: Quagmire I, II, IV (ACA definitions) with an arbitrary alphabet (pair) and a repeating key: the community's open lengths decided exactly by linear certificates mod 2/13 plus complete backtracking with distinct places
k4_result: Two open lengths close for every alphabet: Quagmire I at L=20 (positions 26/66 give x[O]-x[L] = Q-V = -5 and 31/71 give x[A]-x[O] = K-F = +5, so x[A] = x[L]) and Quagmire II at L=13 (seven clue pairs chain y[K] = y[F]+6 = y[S]+2 = ... = y[N]+17 = y[R], so y[K] = y[R]). Backtracking agrees (UNSAT in 8 and 10 steps). Every other listed length is genuinely satisfiable with all places distinct: Quagmire I at 13, 16, 19, 23, 24, 26; Quagmire II at 16, 19, 20, 23, 24, 26; Quagmire IV at 8, 13, 16, 19, 20, 23, 24, 26 (witness alphabets found in 3 to 22,078 steps and checked by re-deriving a consistent key from the full alphabets). Over L=1-26 K4 is closed at 20 lengths for QI, 20 for QII, 18 for QIV. The Vigenere and Beaufort forms give the same verdict at every length for I, II, IV (Beaufort is Vigenere with one keyed alphabet reversed). Quagmire III regression reproduces idea 130 exactly (Vigenere empty at 1-26; Beaufort satisfiable only at 23, 26). Every UNSAT system on K4 has a linear certificate; none needed the search alone.
controls: 50 shuffled K4s, L=1-26, models I, II, IV (Vigenere; first 5 also Beaufort, identical verdicts). SAT counts at the open lengths (K4 in brackets). QI: 13: 10/50 (SAT), 16: 22 (SAT), 19: 1 (SAT), 20: 8 (UNSAT), 23: 30, 24: 46, 26: 49 (all SAT). QII: 13: 22/50 (UNSAT), 16: 34, 19: 2, 20: 20, 23: 36, 24: 45, 26: 49 (all SAT). QIV: 8: 18/50, 13: 37, 16: 41, 19: 2, 20: 36, 23: 39, 24: 46, 26: 49 (all SAT). Closed lengths out of 26: QI K4 20 vs shuffled 18-23 (median 21, 47/50 >= K4); QII K4 20 vs 13-24 (median 19, 20/50 >= K4); QIV K4 18 vs 9-21 (median 15, 8/50 >= K4). K4 being SAT at 19 where 48/50 shuffles are closed is K4's repeated R->P at positions 27 and 65 (38 = 2 x 19 apart), which turns one equation into 0 = 0; it is clue structure, not a signal. 1 control system of 4,290 ran out of the 5M-step budget.
planted: 22/22: one per model and open length (QI 7, QII 7, QIV 8), random alphabet(s), random key, alternating Vigenere/Beaufort, English 97 letters with K4's clue words. Every one SAT, no false certificate, true alphabets satisfy every equation, clue-forced key reads the planted text back.
scope_limits: Decides only whether the 24 carved clue letters are consistent with the model; says nothing about English. The satisfiable lengths stay open: the clues fix few places (1-16 equations), so huge numbers of alphabet pairs fit and only an English search can judge them (QIV at 8 was hill-climbed in idea 113, QI/QII by the community's annealing). Only a plain repeating key, ACA Quagmire I/II/IV definitions, carved clue positions with no gap slack, no transposition layer. Lengths 27+ not run.

negative.hypothesis: K4 is Quagmire I with a repeating key of length 20, or Quagmire II with a repeating key of length 13, for some keyed alphabet.
negative.scope: All 26! keyed alphabets, all keys, Vigenere and Beaufort forms, ACA definitions (QI plain side keyed/cipher A-Z; QII plain A-Z/cipher keyed), carved clue positions 21-33 and 63-73; exact decision by linear algebra mod 2/13 and complete backtracking with distinct places. Also re-decided: QI at 13, 16, 19, 23, 24, 26, QII at 16, 19, 20, 23, 24, 26 and QIV at 8, 13, 16, 19, 20, 23, 24, 26 are satisfiable (not dead).
negative.outcome: Dead: QI at 20 forces x[A] = x[L] (pairs 26/66, 31/71); QII at 13 forces y[K] = y[R] (seven pairs); backtracking agrees. The other open lengths are truly satisfiable and stay open for an English test. (Controls: 42/50 shuffled K4s are also closed for QI at 20 and 28/50 for QII at 13, so these closures are not a signal; planted 22/22 SAT with no false certificate.)

follow_ups: The community table can now be stated exactly: Quagmire I is open only at 13, 16, 19, 23, 24, 26; Quagmire II only at 16, 19, 20, 23, 24, 26; Quagmire IV at 8, 13, 16, 19, 20, 23, 24, 26. None can be closed by the clue letters, so every remaining case needs an English hill-climb with the clue equations kept as hard constraints, judged against shuffled K4s (idea 113 did QIV at 8).

Length 19 is special for all three models: only 1-2 of 50 shuffled K4s survive it, K4 survives only because positions 27 and 65 are both R->P. A QI/QII hill-climb at L=19 with that repeat would be the most constrained of the open cases (8 equations on 11-12 letters).
